title: Seeded-defect corpus row
description: One row of tests/evals/fixtures/seeded-defect/corpus.jsonl: exactly one synthetic defect, expressed as a unified diff against an invented module, plus the single finding a reviewer is expected to produce for it. Draft-07 and not 2020-12 because ajv resolves at 6.x in this repository (package.json devDependencies "ajv": "^6.15.0") and ajv 6 cannot compile 2020-12 - the same constraint tests/evals/fixtures/routebench/baselines.schema.json records. Every object is closed to additional properties: an open object would let a typo-ed key sit in the corpus asserting nothing, which is the fail-open this schema exists to prevent.

id.description: Stable row identity, SD-001..SD-030. A runner joins its input on this, so an id is never reused for a different defect: renumbering silently reassigns every recorded score.

class.description: Defect taxonomy axis. Seven values, each covered by at least three rows. This is the axis a per-class catch rate is broken down by, so it is deliberately coarse - the finer vocabulary is finding_kind.

language.description: Language of the file the diff applies to. Restricted to the five actually present in the corpus rather than an open string, so a sixth language cannot be added without also being argued for in the README distribution table.

file_hint.description: Relative POSIX path of the invented file. Not a path in this repository - every module in this corpus is fabricated. The pattern rejects absolute paths, drive letters and backslashes by construction, and the leading lookahead rejects a '..' segment: a corpus row is fed to a reviewer as text, and a path that resolves out of the fixture directory would invite it to go read a real file.

injected_diff.description: Unified diff with '--- a/<path>', '+++ b/<path>' and one '@@' hunk, at most 40 newline-separated lines. Contains defect-unrelated but legitimate changes as well, so that 'every added line is the defect' is not a winning strategy.

expected.description: The one finding this row is scored against. One row carries exactly one expectation; a diff that would justify two independent findings belongs in two rows.

finding_kind.description: Controlled vocabulary, kebab-case. Enumerates only the kinds some row actually uses - an unused value would be a claim of coverage the corpus does not have. Scoring compares a reviewer's kind to this by exact string equality, so adding a synonym splits the vocabulary rather than widening it.

path.description: Must equal file_hint and the diff's '+++ b/' path. Asserted in the test rather than here: JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare two sibling values.

line_range.description: [start, end] inclusive, numbered in the POST-APPLY (new) file, and required to fall inside the hunk's new range. Post-apply because that is the only numbering a reviewer reading the patched file can produce; pre-apply numbering would score a correct reviewer as wrong on every hunk that adds lines. Some ranges point at a CONTEXT line - a docs-drift row's defect is the unchanged sentence the diff made false.

severity.description: Author's judgement of impact if the defect shipped. Present so a runner can weight or filter; no scoring rule in the README currently reads it.

source.description: Every row is invented. A const rather than an enum: if a row is ever extracted from a real incident it needs its own provenance fields (repository, commit, scrub record), not a second value here.

design_axis.description: OPTIONAL cross-tag to the seven real-incident axes of .artibot/guides/v5-design/ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md:188. Orthogonal to class: class says what kind of mistake the code makes, design_axis says which historical failure mode of THIS repository it rhymes with. Absent on rows that match no axis - the enum lists all seven, and the README records which of them no row currently exercises, because a silently unused value would otherwise read as coverage.
